walkthroughs.body_html:
Both are pure carbon — but very different.

Diamond: each C bonded to 4 others tetrahedrally; sp³. Hardest natural substance, electrical insulator (no free e⁻).

Graphite: each C bonded to 3 others in hexagonal sheets; sp². Layers slide (lubricant), delocalised e⁻ above/below conduct electricity.

Graphene (Geim + Novoselov, Nobel 2010): single sheet of graphite. Strongest material known, transparent, conducts.

Fullerenes like C₆₀ (buckminsterfullerene, 1985): football-shaped molecules. Used in drug delivery, electronics.

Carbon nanotubes: rolled graphene; super strong, conducting.

Mixing s + p orbitals gives equivalent hybrid orbitals:

- sp³ (1s + 3p = 4) — tetrahedral, 109.5°. CH₄, diamond.
- sp² (1s + 2p = 3) — trigonal planar, 120°. C=C in ethene, graphite. Remaining p forms π bond.
- sp (1s + 1p = 2) — linear, 180°. C≡C in ethyne. Two π bonds.

mcqs.q: Which allotrope is one atom thick?
What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.

mcqs.q: If a complex ion has a coordination number of 4, what shape does it have?
options: A coordination number of 4 always means square planar because complexes prefer to be flat.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
It can be either tetrahedral OR square planar — the shape depends on the metal and ligands (e.g. [Pt(NH3)4]2+ is square planar; [CuCl4]2- is tetrahedral).
A coordination number of 4 always means tetrahedral, because that gives the maximum bond-angle separation.

mcqs.q: What does the M+ peak in a mass spectrum represent?
options: The M+ peak shows the mass of the largest fragment after the molecule breaks apart.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The molecular ion — formed when a single electron is removed from the whole molecule, giving the relative molecular mass.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.
